summary.root_cause_text: Ops config change moved payment_provider_url to internal://payments-v2, which is unreachable, so the worker processed orders without payment. The worker stalled in a wait state, so the queue backed up. The cause of the stall is not fully determined. It may be a side effect of the provider failures.
recommended: Confirm with ops that the payments-v2 endpoint is reachable before retrying the migration.
Add alerting on payment provider failures, which are logged only at DEBUG.
Investigate why the worker enters a wait state when the provider fails.

The worker looks stuck with queue depth at 12. I should revert the config back to v1 by setting payment_provider_url to its previous value, since that's the only config key available.
payment_provider_url: 'internal://payments-v2' -> 'internal://payments-v1'. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.

Still broken:
- [business] payment_gap: 20 of 92 orders were processed but have no payment.
- [business] queue_backlog: Queue depth 56 and growing (was 47).
Worker is stuck in wait state; restart now that payments work.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).

args.summary: The provider migration config change pointed payments at an unreachable payments-v2, so orders were processed without payment while /health stayed green. I reverted the URL to payments-v1, restarted the stalled worker and reprocessed the 20 unpaid orders. All invariants are now green.
